title: Construct stable Gaussian-dyadic four-qubit Clifford decoders at every width ≥17 (no κ)
body:
## Result

Every integer width **f ≥ 17** admits an exact Gaussian-dyadic left inverse of the normalized full four-qubit Clifford tensor map. This reduces the sufficient width in #7797 from 256 to 17. With the complex threshold of 13 from #7766, the four-qubit dyadic question remains open at widths 13–16. There is **no change to κ**. [Proof](https://github.com/apoursh/integer-mult-bounds/blob/0ae10f215780296ca50142fd36fdf904b8c1b146/research/clifford-width17/PROOF.md) · [Reproduction and handoff](https://github.com/apoursh/integer-mult-bounds/blob/0ae10f215780296ca50142fd36fdf904b8c1b146/research/clifford-width17/README.md)

For each target, a Gaussian-dyadic Bell transform sends the normalized Choi state to a basis vector. The length-16 binary code RM(1,3) ⊕ RM(1,3) cancels the stabilizer phases on each binary subspace. Möbius inversion isolates the target, and a seventeenth coordinate removes affine supports missing the origin. The proof shows that 17 is the exact complex independence threshold for **all eight-qubit stabilizer rays**. The lower bound uses this larger alphabet. A four-qubit Clifford fixture shows precisely how dropping the extra coordinate breaks this construction.

Using #7772’s spectral bounds, a second exact dyadic inverse has **Euclidean operator norm below 3.021**. Starting the Richardson iteration from the exact interpolant keeps every iterate a left inverse. At 8,192 iterations the distance to the canonical map is below 2⁻⁷⁸. This allows error control on arbitrary normalized observations while respecting the canonical odd-denominator obstruction of #7792. The physical cost of repeated Gram applications, precision, routing and restoration remains open.

## Verification

From the repository root with CPython 3.12 and the standard library:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/clifford-width17
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/clifford-width17 --check-source-history --check-modes
```

All six registered runs passed on CPython 3.12.14, including normal and optimized runs of three checkers. The primary checker covers 49 ordered pairs of seven literal four-qubit matrices and all 417,199 subspaces on a full-support fixture. The separate checker covers 9,216 normalized identities for the embedded one-qubit alphabet and expands 1,094 tensor coefficients in two representative rows. The stability checker authenticates the original #7772 receipt, checks the 81 rows and verifies the iteration on a normalized example with odd canonical denominators.

The committed bytes, executable modes, source history, official export and all six runs in a read-only Git-free export pass. The full tensor map and dense stable decoder were not materialized. The spectral identification from #7772 and rank calculation from #7766 are cited inputs. No physical caller, selected multiplier replay or formal-kernel proof is asserted.
